producedBy.recipe: the full height and 1386 of the 6000 columns about column 3005, each row drawn in the sinusoidal projection about that column: a pixel x on a row at galactic latitude b averages the panorama's row over the 1/cos(b) columns about 3005 + (x - 693)/cos(b), wrapping round the sky; written as JPEG at quality 92 (.lanetools/homeedge/reproject.py in the MOBILE lane, home-edge-and-name-one)

files.note: The region of the approved iPhone home capture (arrive p-home and phone3 c-home, crop mw-tall.jpg 780 by 1688), found by normalised cross-correlation on luminance at 0.944 (.lanetools/match_tall.py): left 0.3853, top 0.0013, 0.2301 of the width, 0.9959 of the height. The equirectangular rows stretch every star sideways by 1/cos(b) toward the poles, which the home's top edge showed; the sinusoidal projection draws them as points (home-edge-and-name-one). On the galactic equator it is the crop itself; toward the top and the foot each row reaches farther along the sky. The app darkens it toward the bottom as the capture does.
